taskDescription: Arrange the stages of the human louse life cycle in the correct chronological order.
paragraphs: The female louse cements her eggs (nits) to hair shafts or clothing fibres using chitinous glue
The egg hatches into a nymph after 7 to 10 days
The nymph matures through three successive nymphal stages over 9 to 12 days
The fully mature adult louse emerges and begins blood-feeding on the human host
The adult female lives for 3 to 4 weeks, laying several eggs daily to continue the cycle
